text: Enumerate every canonical registered sequence exactly once and preserve its registry identity, sequence folder, declared automation, operation kinds, and lineage.

source.user_intent: The intake migration must include commit/push sequences, deploy sequences, and every other registered sequence.

acceptance_intent: The inventory row count and sequence-id set exactly match the canonical registry, with no omitted commit, push, deploy, composed, or sub-sequence row.

planner_obligations.description: Use the frozen complete registry inventory as the migration scope; no sequence family may be inferred away.

text: Resolve every registered sequence to its actual locally available automation entrypoint or explicitly classify it as composed, human-only, MCP-backed, unavailable, or unresolved.

source.user_intent: The reusable intake must be called by each real script rather than by a partial list of wrappers.

acceptance_intent: Every registry row has grounded repository/path evidence for all operational entrypoints, or a visible evidence limitation instead of a guessed path.

planner_obligations.description: Plan against actual executable ownership and explicitly handle composed, MCP-backed, human-only, unavailable, and unresolved cases.

text: Classify the complete current input surface of every resolved entrypoint, including positional arguments, flags, environment variables, files, stdin, prompts, embedded command text, defaults, and no-argument behavior.

source.user_intent: The model must only answer format-guided questions; intake code must build the final JSON or argument structure.

acceptance_intent: Each resolved entrypoint has a source-grounded input classification and identifies exactly where the model currently authors structured or free-form invocation data.

planner_obligations.description: Preserve every real input source and eliminate model-authored JSON, argv, flag, and command-envelope construction from operator-facing invocation.

text: Inventory every authoritative call site or operator instruction that invokes a registered entrypoint and determine whether it can bypass the no-argument intake boundary.

source.user_intent: A reusable intake only works if every actual sequence invocation reaches it.

acceptance_intent: Every authoritative invocation surface is identified, including stale direct-command examples and legacy argument-bearing paths that could bypass intake.

planner_obligations.description: Migrate or deliberately contain every authoritative bypass so normal operator use starts at the no-argument entrypoint.

text: Define the future operator-facing contract for every migratable entrypoint: launch with no arguments, ask one question at a time, show response format, example, and constraints, and let deterministic intake code construct the final typed JSON or argv payload.

source.user_intent: The agent answers questions only; it never constructs the JSON envelope, and every question explains the required response format with an example.

acceptance_intent: For each applicable entrypoint, a no-argument invocation can deterministically collect valid answers and produce the exact internal structure without asking the model to author JSON, argv, flags, or shell syntax.

planner_obligations.description: Plan one shared intake contract and a grounded per-entrypoint schema, adapter, and verification case for every applicable registered automation.

text: Preserve effect authorization separately from deterministic intake construction for commit, push, deploy, authentication, database, container, package, cleanup, remote-operator, and workflow-drive sequences.

source.user_intent: Input construction should become reliable without silently broadening authority to execute effectful operations.

acceptance_intent: Intake may prepare and validate the exact operation manifest, but effectful dispatch still requires the existing explicit approval, review, dry-run, or guard boundary appropriate to that sequence.

planner_obligations.description: Keep deterministic parameter construction and effect authorization as separate, testable states for every high-impact sequence class.

text: Identify repository ownership, local availability, implementation scope, compatibility needs, and verification constraints for migrating all registered automation without executing live effects.

source.user_intent: The next implementation must be complete across repositories and reviewable before commit, push, or deployment.

acceptance_intent: The planner receives a repository-by-repository implementation surface, known compatibility consumers, safe static/unit verification options, and explicit live-verification approval gates.

planner_obligations.description: Sequence the implementation by repository and risk while retaining legacy compatibility only where grounded consumers require it.
